surface: PostgreSQL 16.15 behaviour through the redlinedb SQL shell with REDLINEDB_RESULT_DIALECT=postgres
evidence: The beyond_sqlite corpus runs each case in a fresh redlinedb process on :memory: and compares its normalized SQL-shell transcript with psql against the pinned PostgreSQL 16.15 server. A case outcome (positive_match, expected_rejection, declared_unsupported, mismatch) says what one script printed. The status below says what the product supports. A case that matches the transcript is not, by itself, support for the capability it touches.

statuses.implemented: Behaves as PostgreSQL does for the stated surface, and corpus cases would fail otherwise.
statuses.partial: Part of the surface works; the note names the part that does not.
statuses.unsupported: Absent, rejected, or answered by a stand-in that does not perform the operation.
statuses.unverified: No lane exercises it; no claim either way.

capabilities.surface: PostgreSQL frontend/backend protocol (psql, libpq and PostgreSQL drivers)
capabilities.note: redlinedb-server speaks its own RLDB framing, not the PostgreSQL protocol, so psql and PostgreSQL drivers cannot connect. The corpus drives the redlinedb CLI.
There is no PostgreSQL listener, so there is no PostgreSQL TLS. redlinedb-server has no TLS either.

capabilities.surface: Roles and authorization: CREATE ROLE, GRANT, REVOKE, ownership checks, row security
capabilities.note: There is one implicit role, redlinedb. current_user, OWNER TO CURRENT_USER and CREATE SCHEMA ... AUTHORIZATION CURRENT_USER report it (the cited cases); current_user, session_user, current_role and pg_get_userbyid exist only in the Postgres dialect. CREATE ROLE and GRANT fail as unsupported SQL, and no statement is authorization-checked.

capabilities.surface: SQLSTATE codes and PostgreSQL error fields (DETAIL, HINT, position)
capabilities.note: The shell prints RedlineDB error codes and English text; no SQLSTATE is produced. Expected rejections match on declared error text, not on SQLSTATE.

capabilities.surface: NOTIFY and pg_notify delivery to listening sessions
capabilities.note: NOTIFY is refused when it is prepared, and pg_notify when it is called, with unsupported capability: nothing delivers a notification, so the cited cases are declared unsupported (PG-01). Before, NOTIFY was a no-op and pg_notify returned without delivering anything, and both answered in the default SQLite dialect too. LISTEN and UNLISTEN keep a channel set per connection (cases 20430, 20433, 20434, 20439, 20440), and pg_notification_queue_usage() is 0 because nothing can be queued (case 20436).

Session-level exclusive locks shared by the connections of one open database in one process and owned by the connection that took them (PG-01): pg_try_advisory_lock answers f while another connection holds the key, pg_advisory_lock waits up to the busy timeout and then fails with lock timeout, pg_advisory_unlock answers t only for a key this connection holds, locks nest, and pg_advisory_unlock_all or dropping the connection releases them. The bigint and (int, int) keys are separate key spaces; the void result prints as an empty cell. Not provided: the shared and transaction-level variants, locks between processes, and the WARNING PostgreSQL prints for an unheld key. Two-connection tests are in crates/sql/tests/pg_behavior_two_sessions.rs; the cited cases run in one session.

Both return the id of the statement's transaction (PG-01): the same value throughout BEGIN ... COMMIT, a different one in every transaction, including concurrent ones and each autocommit statement, and never reused. Differences from PostgreSQL: every transaction has an id from its start, read-only ones included; the ids are RedlineDB's own transaction counter, not 32-bit xids with an epoch; and pg_current_xact_id returns a bigint, not xid8. The cited cases check only that the value is a positive integer.

pg_current_wal_lsn is refused with unsupported capability: the WAL position is not exposed to SQL, so cases 20416 and 20417 are declared unsupported (PG-01). pg_wal_lsn_diff is arithmetic on two LSN literals: the signed byte distance ('0/10' minus '0/0' is 16, the reverse -16), invalid input syntax for type pg_lsn for a malformed LSN, and unsupported capability for a distance outside the bigint range. With no LSN source, that arithmetic is all it offers.
pg_export_snapshot is refused with unsupported capability: no other session can import a snapshot, so case 20423 is declared unsupported (PG-01). SET TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT is not supported.

capabilities.surface: Logical decoding, replication slots, publications and subscriptions (CDC)
capabilities.note: Cases 20418 and 20429 are expected rejections: both engines refuse logical decoding while wal_level is replica. The other cited cases count empty catalog shims or accept DDL that replicates nothing.
Case 20340 is an expected rejection: CREATE EXTENSION vector fails with extension "vector" is not available on both engines.

Values cast with ::citext compare and order without case in =, <, ORDER BY and DISTINCT (the cited cases). A column declared citext is refused with unsupported capability: citext column, because it would compare with case. The cast prefixes the value with U+E000, which length, octet_length and substr count ('Hello'::citext has length 6). count(DISTINCT), GROUP BY and indexes still compare cast values by their bytes. The prefix means "without case" only in Postgres-dialect statements after CREATE EXTENSION citext; everywhere else, including every SQLite-dialect connection, U+E000 is an ordinary character (PG-03).

capabilities.surface: Behaviour across sessions: locks, notifications, snapshots and catalog visibility between connections
capabilities.note: Every corpus case runs in one fresh process on :memory:, so no corpus case observes a second session, and no lane compares two sessions with PostgreSQL. Native two-connection tests (crates/sql/tests/pg_behavior_two_sessions.rs, PG-08) check that advisory locks contend and are released when a connection drops, LISTEN channel sets are per connection, NOTIFY is refused, concurrent transactions have distinct txid_current values, tables, indexes and views one connection creates are in the other's pg_class, and a refreshed materialized view is refreshed for both. Known gaps: sequences and the pg_matviews catalog are kept per connection, so a second connection cannot call nextval on a sequence the first one created (pinned by that file), and pg_backend_pid() is the OS process id, the same for every connection (case 20408 checks only that it is stable and positive).
